The signature is associated with the data directory CERTIFICATE\_TABLE that is not always tied to a section (it implies that the signature is not necessarily mapped in memory). In fact, the data directory entry points to a file offset, not a RVA. This signature is wrapped in a PKCS #7 container with custom object types as defined in the official documentation \[1\].<br/><br/>This signature is not new in PE files and since the beginning of LIEF, we aimed to parse it. Before the version v0.11.0, the implementation was somehow incomplete and inaccurate but since the version v0.11.0 and thanks to the sponsoring of the CERT Gouvernemental of Luxembourg, we refactored the design of the authenticode parser \[2\] and we implemented functions to verify the signature.<br/><br/>## Exploring PKCS #7 Signature¶<br/><br/>LIEF API tries to expose most of the internal components of the PKCS #7 container associated with the Authenticode. First, we can access the PE’s signature through the lief.PE.Binary.signatures attribute \[3\]:<br/><br/>import lief<br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(len(pe.signatures))<br/><br/>signature = pe.signatures[0]<br/><br/>Although we usually find only **one** signature, PE executables can embed multiple signatures thanks to the `/as` command of `signtool.exe`. This is why the signatures attribute returns an **iterator** over the signatures parsed by LIEF.<br/><br/>The signature variable is actually a lief.PE.Signature object which basically mirrors the PKCS #7 container plus some method to verify its integrity.<br/><br/>Within this object, we can access the following attributes:<br/><br/>* x509 certificates used to sign the executable: lief.PE.Signature.certificates<br/>* The ContentInfo object that contains the authentihash value: lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest<br/>* The SignerInfo structure: lief.PE.Signature.signers  <br/>Note  <br/>While the PKCS #7 standard enables multiple signers, Microsoft specifications require **one** and **only one** signer.<br/><br/>The `__str__()` functions of these objects are overloaded so that we can pretty-print the content of these objects easily:<br/><br/># Print certificates information<br/>for crt in signature.certificates:<br/>  print(crt)<br/><br/># Print the authentihash value embedded in the signature<br/>print(signature.content_info.digest.hex())<br/><br/># Print signer information<br/>print(signature.signers[0])<br/><br/>cert. version     : 3<br/>serial number     :  Generic Type 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1 (MS_COUNTER_SIGN)<br/><br/>## Verifying the Signature¶<br/><br/>Besides the fact that LIEF can parse PE’s authenticode signature, LIEF can also verify the integrity of the authentihash thanks to the method: lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature() which outputs lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS.OK if the signature is valid or another enum (see: lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS) when it is invalid:<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature()) # lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK<br/><br/>We can also verify a PE binary with a **detached signature** by providing a signature object to verify\_signature():<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/><br/>detached_sig = lief.PE.Signature.parse("/tmp/detached.p7b")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature(detached_sig))<br/><br/>The verification process does not rely on an external component (i.e. neither openssl nor WinTrust API) but we try to reproduce the same checks as described in the RFC(s) and the official documentation of the Authenticode \[4\].<br/><br/>These checks include:<br/><br/>1. Check the integrity of the signature (lief.PE.Signature.check()):  <br/>   1. There is ONE and only ONE SignerInfo  <br/>   2. Digest algorithms are consistent (Signature.digest\_algorithm `==` ContentInfo.digest\_algorithm `==` SignerInfo.digest\_algorithm)  <br/>   3. If the SignerInfo has authenticated attributes, check their integrity. Otherwise, check the integrity of the ContentInfo against the Signer’s certificate.  <br/>   4. If there are authenticated attributes, check that there is a lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest attribute for which the digest matches the hash of the ContentInfo  <br/>   5. If there is a counter signature in the **un-authenticated attributes**, verify its integrity and check that it wraps a valid _timestamping_.  <br/>   6. Check the expiration of the certificates according to the potential _timestamping_<br/>2. If the signature is valid, check that lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest matches the computed authentihash()<br/><br/>These checks are the default behavior of the verify\_signature(). Nevertheless, you could pass lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_CHECKS flags to customize its behavior:<br/><br/>Hash Only:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.HASH\_ONLY, it only performs step `B)` (i.e. check the authentihash values regardless of the signature integrity)<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.HASH_ONLY)<br/><br/>Lifetime Signing:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.LIFETIME\_SIGNING, timestamped signatures can expire if their certificate expired. It has the same meaning as WTD\_LIFETIME\_SIGNING\_FLAG<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/><br/>Skip Certificate Check Time:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.SKIP\_CERT\_TIME, LIEF doesn’t raise an error if the certificate(s) expired.<br/><br/># Returns lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK even though<br/># the certificates expired<br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To verify the integrity of a Signature object, you can use lief.PE.Signature.check()<br/><br/>## Certificate Chain of Trust¶<br/><br/>Last but not least, we can also verify the certificates chain thanks to:<br/><br/>1. lief.PE.x509.verify()<br/>2. lief.PE.x509.is\_trusted\_by()<br/><br/>verify() aims to verify a signed certificate from its CA. Given a CA x509 certificate, `CA.verify(signed)` verifies that the `signed` parameter has been signed by `CA`.<br/><br/>On the other hand, is\_trusted\_by() can be used to check that a given x509 certificate is verified against a **list of certificates**:<br/><br/>CA_BUNDLE = lief.PE.x509.parse("ms_bundle.pem")<br/>signer = signature.signers[0]<br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by(CA_BUNDLE))<br/><br/>cert1 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca1.crt")<br/>cert2 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca2.crt")<br/><br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by([cert1, cert2]))<br/><br/>## Limitations¶<br/><br/>Regarding the PKCS #7 structure itself, LIEF is able to parse and process most of its elements. Nevertheless, the lief.PE.SignerInfo structure can embed attributes (authenticated or not) for which the ASN.1 structure can be public or not. As of LIEF v0.11.0 we do not support yet the following OIDs:<br/><br/>\| OID                        \| Description                                                      \|<br/>\| -------------------------- \| ---------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1      \| Ms-CounterSign (undocumented, supported in LIEF 0.15.0)          \|<br/>\| 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.2.12 \| S/MIME Signing certificate (id-aa-signingCertificate)            \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.6.1      \| SPC\_COMMERCIAL\_SP\_KEY\_PURPOSE\_OBJID                         \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.28    \| szOID\_PLATFORM\_MANIFEST\_BINARY\_ID (supported in LIEF 0.15.0) \|<br/><br/>These not-supported attributes are wrapped within the lief.PE.GenericType that exposes the raw ASN.1 blob with the property raw\_content.<br/><br/>## Conclusion¶<br/><br/>Under the hood, most of the work is done by mbedtls which provides the following primitive used by LIEF:<br/><br/>* ASN.1 decoder<br/>* x509 certificate processing (parsing AND verification)<br/>* Hash algorithms<br/>* Public key algorithms<br/><br/>We can also cross-compile a small C++ snippet for iOS:<br/><br/>#include <LIEF/PE.hpp><br/><br/>int main(int argc, char** argv) \{<br/>  std::unique_ptr<LIEF::PE::Binary> pe = LIEF::PE::Parser::parse(argv[1])<br/>  if (pe->verify_signature() == LIEF::PE::Signature::VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK) \{<br/>    std::cout << "Signature ok!" << "\n";<br/>    return 0;<br/>  \}<br/>  std::cout << "Error!" << "\n";<br/>  return 1;<br/>\}<br/><br/>So that we can verify the integrity of a PE executable on an iPhone:<br/><br/>iPhone:~ root# file PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows<br/>iPhone:~ root# file ./pe_authenticode_check<br/>./pe_authenticode_check: Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, flags:<NOUNDEFS\|DYLDLINK\|TWOLEVEL\|WEAK_DEFINES\|BINDS_TO_WEAK\|PIE\|HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS><br/>iPhone:~ root# ./pe_authenticode_check PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>Signature ok!<br/>iPhone:~ root#<br/><br/>Whilst this example is quite useless, it emphasizes the purpose of this project:<br/><br/>* Provide a cross-platform and cross-format library<br/>* Expose a high-level API (Python) as well as a (more or less) low-level API (C++)<br/>* Few dependencies so that the static version of LIEF does not need external libraries \[5\].<br/><br/>$ otool -L pe_authenticode_check<br/><br/>/System/Library/Frameworks/Foundation.framework/Foundation (compatibility version 300.0.0, current version 1770.255.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 228.0.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 904.4.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1292.60.1)<br/><br/>To complete these functionalities of LIEF, you might also be interested in the following projects that deal with Authenticode:<br/><br/>\| Project          \| URL                                                                            \|<br/>\| ---------------- \| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ \|<br/>\| signify          \| <https://github.com/ralphje/signify>                                           \|<br/>\| winsign          \| <https://github.com/mozilla-releng/winsign>                                    \|<br/>\| uthenticode      \| <https://github.com/trailofbits/uthenticode>                                   \|<br/>\| AuthenticodeLint \| <https://github.com/vcsjones/AuthenticodeLint>                                 \|<br/>\| osslsigncode     \| <https://github.com/mtrojnar/osslsigncode>                                     \|<br/>\| yara-x           \| <https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x> (which has support for PE Authenticode) \|<br/><br/>Finally, you can find additional information about the Authenticode in Trail of Bits blog post \[6\]. If you are interested in Authenticode tricks used by Dropbox, you can take a look at Microsoft website \[7\] and if you are interested in understanding how the integrity of the PKCS #7 works, you can look at _Manual verify PKCS#7 signed data with OpenSSL_ \[8\]<br/><br/>References<br/><br/>\[1\]<br/><br/><http://download.microsoft.com/download/9/c/5/9c5b2167-8017-4bae-9fde-d599bac8184a/Authenticode%5FPE.docx><br/><br/>\[2\]<br/><br/>Which now exceptions-free<br/><br/>\[3\]<br/><br/>This tutorial uses the Python API but the C++ API is very similar<br/><br/>\[4\]<br/><br/>See: src/PE/signature/Signature.cpp - check() for the implementation<br/><br/>\[5\]<br/><br/>Except the C/C++ STL<br/><br/>\[6\]<br/><br/><https://blog.trailofbits.com/2020/05/27/verifying-windows-binaries-without-windows/><br/><br/>\[7\]<br/><br/><https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/ieinternals/caveats-for-authenticode-code-signing><br/><br/>\[8\]<br/><br/><http://qistoph.blogspot.com/2012/01/manual-verify-pkcs7-signed-data-with.html><br/><br/>API<br/><br/>* lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_md5<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha1<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha256<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha512<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.signatures<br/>* lief.PE.Signature<br/>* lief.PE.x509<br/>* lief.PE.ContentInfo<br/>* lief.PE.SignerInfo<br/>* lief.PE.Attribute<br/>* lief.PE.ContentType<br/>* lief.PE.GenericType<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcNestedSignature<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcStatementType<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9AtSequenceNumber<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9CounterSignature<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9SigningTime<br/>* lief.PE.SpcSpOpusInfo<br/><br/> On this page: IntroductionExploring PKCS #7 SignatureVerifying the SignatureCertificate Chain of TrustLimitationsConclusion |

The signature is associated with the data directory CERTIFICATE\_TABLE that is not always tied to a section (it implies that the signature is not necessarily mapped in memory). In fact, the data directory entry points to a file offset, not a RVA. This signature is wrapped in a PKCS #7 container with custom object types as defined in the official documentation \[1\].<br/><br/>This signature is not new in PE files and since the beginning of LIEF, we aimed to parse it. Before the version v0.11.0, the implementation was somehow incomplete and inaccurate but since the version v0.11.0 and thanks to the sponsoring of the CERT Gouvernemental of Luxembourg, we refactored the design of the authenticode parser \[2\] and we implemented functions to verify the signature.<br/><br/>## Exploring PKCS #7 Signature¶<br/><br/>LIEF API tries to expose most of the internal components of the PKCS #7 container associated with the Authenticode. First, we can access the PE’s signature through the lief.PE.Binary.signatures attribute \[3\]:<br/><br/>import lief<br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(len(pe.signatures))<br/><br/>signature = pe.signatures[0]<br/><br/>Although we usually find only **one** signature, PE executables can embed multiple signatures thanks to the `/as` command of `signtool.exe`. This is why the signatures attribute returns an **iterator** over the signatures parsed by LIEF.<br/><br/>The signature variable is actually a lief.PE.Signature object which basically mirrors the PKCS #7 container plus some method to verify its integrity.<br/><br/>Within this object, we can access the following attributes:<br/><br/>* x509 certificates used to sign the executable: lief.PE.Signature.certificates<br/>* The ContentInfo object that contains the authentihash value: lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest<br/>* The SignerInfo structure: lief.PE.Signature.signers  <br/>Note  <br/>While the PKCS #7 standard enables multiple signers, Microsoft specifications require **one** and **only one** signer.<br/><br/>The `__str__()` functions of these objects are overloaded so that we can pretty-print the content of these objects easily:<br/><br/># Print certificates information<br/>for crt in signature.certificates:<br/>  print(crt)<br/><br/># Print the authentihash value embedded in the signature<br/>print(signature.content_info.digest.hex())<br/><br/># Print signer information<br/>print(signature.signers[0])<br/><br/>cert. version     : 3<br/>serial number     : 04:09:18:1B:5F:D5:BB:66:75:53:43:B5:6F:95:50:08<br/>issuer name       : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert Assured ID Root CA<br/>subject name      : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>issued  on        : 2013-10-22 12:00:00<br/>expires on        : 2028-10-22 12:00:00<br/>signed using      : RSA with SHA-256<br/>RSA key size      : 2048 bits<br/>basic constraints : CA=true, max_pathlen=0<br/>key usage         : Digital Signature, Key Cert Sign, CRL Sign<br/>ext key usage     : Code Signing<br/><br/>cert. version     : 3<br/>serial number     : 09:70:EF:4B:AD:5C:C4:4A:1C:2B:C3:D9:64:01:67:4C<br/>issuer name       : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>subject name      : C=CZ, L=Praha, O=Avast Software s.r.o., OU=RE stapler cistodc, CN=Avast Software s.r.o.<br/>issued  on        : 2020-04-02 00:00:00<br/>expires on        : 2023-03-09 12:00:00<br/>signed using      : RSA with SHA-256<br/>RSA key size      : 2048 bits<br/>basic constraints : CA=false<br/>key usage         : Digital Signature<br/>ext key usage     : Code Signing<br/><br/>a738da4446a4e78ab647db7e53427eb07961c994317f4c59d7edbea5cc786d80<br/>SHA_256/RSA - C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA - 4 auth attr - 1 unauth attr<br/><br/>Regarding the PE files, the authentihash is computed through the function lief.PE.Binary.authentihash() which takes a lief.PE.ALGORITHMS enum as parameter to define which hash algorithm must be used to compute the digest.<br/><br/>For instance, to compute the SHA-256 value of the authenticode, we just have to pass lief.PE.ALGORITHMS.SHA\_256:<br/><br/>print(pe.authentihash(lief.PE.ALGORITHMS.SHA_256).hex())<br/><br/>a738da4446a4e78ab647db7e53427eb07961c994317f4c59d7edbea5cc786d80<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To compare the lief.PE.Binary.authentihash() value with the signed one (i.e. lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest) we must use the same hash algorithm as defined by lief.PE.Signature.digest\_algorithm<br/><br/>We also expose shortcut attributes in the Python API to compute the authentihash values for:<br/><br/>\| Hash Algorithm \| Binary’s Attribute                                                                                                          \|<br/>\| -------------- \| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| MD5            \| [authentihash\_md5](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fmd5 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_md5")          \|<br/>\| SHA1           \| [authentihash\_sha1](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha1 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha1")       \|<br/>\| SHA-256        \| [authentihash\_sha256](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha256 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha256") \|<br/>\| SHA-512        \| [authentihash\_sha512](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha512 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha512") \|<br/><br/>LIEF also exposes the original raw signature blob through the property lief.PE.Signature.raw\_der which enables to export the signature:<br/><br/>from pathlib import Path<br/><br/>Path("/tmp/extracted.p7b").write_bytes(signature.raw_der)<br/><br/>Then, we can (INDIVIDUAL_CODE_SIGNING)<br/>     Info: http://www.avast.com<br/>     PKCS9 Message Digest: 3983816a7d1c62962540ec66fa8790fa45d1063cb23e933677de459f0b73c577<br/>  Un-authenticated attributes:<br/>     Generic Type 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1 (MS_COUNTER_SIGN)<br/><br/>## Verifying the Signature¶<br/><br/>Besides the fact that LIEF can parse PE’s authenticode signature, LIEF can also verify the integrity of the authentihash thanks to the method: lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature() which outputs lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS.OK if the signature is valid or another enum (see: lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS) when it is invalid:<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature()) # lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK<br/><br/>We can also verify a PE binary with a **detached signature** by providing a signature object to verify\_signature():<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/><br/>detached_sig = lief.PE.Signature.parse("/tmp/detached.p7b")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature(detached_sig))<br/><br/>The verification process does not rely on an external component (i.e. neither openssl nor WinTrust API) but we try to reproduce the same checks as described in the RFC(s) and the official documentation of the Authenticode \[4\].<br/><br/>These checks include:<br/><br/>1. Check the integrity of the signature (lief.PE.Signature.check()):  <br/>   1. There is ONE and only ONE SignerInfo  <br/>   2. Digest algorithms are consistent (Signature.digest\_algorithm `==` ContentInfo.digest\_algorithm `==` SignerInfo.digest\_algorithm)  <br/>   3. If the SignerInfo has authenticated attributes, check their integrity. Otherwise, check the integrity of the ContentInfo against the Signer’s certificate.  <br/>   4. If there are authenticated attributes, check that there is a lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest attribute for which the digest matches the hash of the ContentInfo  <br/>   5. If there is a counter signature in the **un-authenticated attributes**, verify its integrity and check that it wraps a valid _timestamping_.  <br/>   6. Check the expiration of the certificates according to the potential _timestamping_<br/>2. If the signature is valid, check that lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest matches the computed authentihash()<br/><br/>These checks are the default behavior of the verify\_signature(). Nevertheless, you could pass lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_CHECKS flags to customize its behavior:<br/><br/>Hash Only:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.HASH\_ONLY, it only performs step `B)` (i.e. check the authentihash values regardless of the signature integrity)<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.HASH_ONLY)<br/><br/>Lifetime Signing:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.LIFETIME\_SIGNING, timestamped signatures can expire if their certificate expired. It has the same meaning as WTD\_LIFETIME\_SIGNING\_FLAG<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/><br/>Skip Certificate Check Time:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.SKIP\_CERT\_TIME, LIEF doesn’t raise an error if the certificate(s) expired.<br/><br/># Returns lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK even though<br/># the certificates expired<br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To verify the integrity of a Signature object, you can use lief.PE.Signature.check()<br/><br/>## Certificate Chain of Trust¶<br/><br/>Last but not least, we can also verify the certificates chain thanks to:<br/><br/>1. lief.PE.x509.verify()<br/>2. lief.PE.x509.is\_trusted\_by()<br/><br/>verify() aims to verify a signed certificate from its CA. Given a CA x509 certificate, `CA.verify(signed)` verifies that the `signed` parameter has been signed by `CA`.<br/><br/>On the other hand, is\_trusted\_by() can be used to check that a given x509 certificate is verified against a **list of certificates**:<br/><br/>CA_BUNDLE = lief.PE.x509.parse("ms_bundle.pem")<br/>signer = signature.signers[0]<br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by(CA_BUNDLE))<br/><br/>cert1 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca1.crt")<br/>cert2 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca2.crt")<br/><br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by([cert1, cert2]))<br/><br/>## Limitations¶<br/><br/>Regarding the PKCS #7 structure itself, LIEF is able to parse and process most of its elements. Nevertheless, the lief.PE.SignerInfo structure can embed attributes (authenticated or not) for which the ASN.1 structure can be public or not. As of LIEF v0.11.0 we do not support yet the following OIDs:<br/><br/>\| OID                        \| Description                                                      \|<br/>\| -------------------------- \| ---------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1      \| Ms-CounterSign (undocumented, supported in LIEF 0.15.0)          \|<br/>\| 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.2.12 \| S/MIME Signing certificate (id-aa-signingCertificate)            \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.6.1      \| SPC\_COMMERCIAL\_SP\_KEY\_PURPOSE\_OBJID                         \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.28    \| szOID\_PLATFORM\_MANIFEST\_BINARY\_ID (supported in LIEF 0.15.0) \|<br/><br/>These not-supported attributes are wrapped within the lief.PE.GenericType that exposes the raw ASN.1 blob with the property raw\_content.<br/><br/>## Conclusion¶<br/><br/>Under the hood, most of the work is done by mbedtls which provides the following primitive used by LIEF:<br/><br/>* ASN.1 decoder<br/>* x509 certificate processing (parsing AND verification)<br/>* Hash algorithms<br/>* Public key algorithms<br/><br/>We can also cross-compile a small C++ snippet for iOS:<br/><br/>#include <LIEF/PE.hpp><br/><br/>int main(int argc, char** argv) \{<br/>  std::unique_ptr<LIEF::PE::Binary> pe = LIEF::PE::Parser::parse(argv[1])<br/>  if (pe->verify_signature() == LIEF::PE::Signature::VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK) \{<br/>    std::cout << "Signature ok!" << "\n";<br/>    return 0;<br/>  \}<br/>  std::cout << "Error!" << "\n";<br/>  return 1;<br/>\}<br/><br/>So that we can verify the integrity of a PE executable on an iPhone:<br/><br/>iPhone:~ root# file PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows<br/>iPhone:~ root# file ./pe_authenticode_check<br/>./pe_authenticode_check: Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, flags:<NOUNDEFS\|DYLDLINK\|TWOLEVEL\|WEAK_DEFINES\|BINDS_TO_WEAK\|PIE\|HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS><br/>iPhone:~ root# ./pe_authenticode_check PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>Signature ok!<br/>iPhone:~ root#<br/><br/>Whilst this example is quite useless, it emphasizes the purpose of this project:<br/><br/>* Provide a cross-platform and cross-format library<br/>* Expose a high-level API (Python) as well as a (more or less) low-level API (C++)<br/>* Few dependencies so that the static version of LIEF does not need external libraries \[5\].<br/><br/>$ otool -L pe_authenticode_check<br/><br/>/System/Library/Frameworks/Foundation.framework/Foundation (compatibility version 300.0.0, current version 1770.255.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 228.0.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 904.4.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1292.60.1)<br/><br/>To complete these functionalities of LIEF, you might also be interested in the following projects that deal with Authenticode:<br/><br/>\| Project          \| URL                                                                            \|<br/>\| ---------------- \| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ \|<br/>\| signify          \| <https://github.com/ralphje/signify>                                           \|<br/>\| winsign          \| <https://github.com/mozilla-releng/winsign>                                    \|<br/>\| uthenticode      \| <https://github.com/trailofbits/uthenticode>                         \|<br/>\| yara-x           \| <https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x> (which has support for PE Authenticode) \|<br/><br/>Finally, you can find additional information about the Authenticode in Trail of Bits blog post \[6\]. If you are interested in Authenticode tricks used by Dropbox, you can take a look at Microsoft website \[7\] and if you are interested in understanding how the integrity of the PKCS #7 works, you can look at _Manual verify PKCS#7 signed data with OpenSSL_ \[8\]<br/><br/>References<br/><br/>\[1\]<br/><br/><http://download.microsoft.com/download/9/c/5/9c5b2167-8017-4bae-9fde-d599bac8184a/Authenticode%5FPE.docx><br/><br/>\[2\]<br/><br/>Which now exceptions-free<br/><br/>\[3\]<br/><br/>This tutorial uses the Python API but the C++ API is very similar<br/><br/>\[4\]<br/><br/>See: src/PE/signature/Signature.cpp - check() for the implementation<br/><br/>\[5\]<br/><br/>Except the C/C++ STL<br/><br/>\[6\]<br/><br/><https://blog.trailofbits.com/2020/05/27/verifying-windows-binaries-without-windows/><br/><br/>\[7\]<br/><br/><https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/ieinternals/caveats-for-authenticode-code-signing><br/><br/>\[8\]<br/><br/><http://qistoph.blogspot.com/2012/01/manual-verify-pkcs7-signed-data-with.html><br/><br/>API<br/><br/>* lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_md5<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha1<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha256<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha512<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.signatures<br/>* lief.PE.Signature<br/>* lief.PE.x509<br/>* lief.PE.ContentInfo<br/>* lief.PE.SignerInfo<br/>* lief.PE.Attribute<br/>* lief.PE.ContentType<br/>* lief.PE.GenericType<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcNestedSignature<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcStatementType<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9AtSequenceNumber<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9CounterSignature<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9SigningTime<br/>* lief.PE.SpcSpOpusInfo<br/><br/> On this page: IntroductionExploring PKCS #7 SignatureVerifying the SignatureCertificate Chain of TrustLimitationsConclusion |

The PDF is not signed until saved to file, steam or byte array.<br/>doc.SaveAs("signed.pdf")<br/><br/># Digital Signatures<br/><br/>This Python code demonstrates how to use a PDF library, such as `PyPDF2`, to cryptographically sign an existing PDF and create a PDF with a digital signature.<br/><br/>## How to Generate a Digital Signature in Python<br/><br/>1. **Download a Python module to generate a digital signature.**  <br/>You can use libraries like `PyPDF2` and `PyPDF4`, which are Python libraries for reading and writing PDF files, but for signing you might prefer something like `reportlab` in combination with `PyPDF2` for digital signatures.<br/>2. **Render a new PDF document.**  <br/>Use `reportlab` to create a new PDF or modify an existing one.<br/>3. **Instantiate the `PdfSignature` class and import the digital certificate.**  <br/>The code snippet below shows how you might do it using a hypothetical `PdfSignature` class. Replace it with the actual method of adding a signature from the library you choose.<br/>4. **Add additional information as needed.**  <br/>Specify metadata, appearance, or location for the signature.<br/>5. **Use the `sign` method to sign the document.**  <br/>Below is a Python code using `reportlab` to create a PDF and `PyPDF2` to attach a digital signature.<br/><br/>```python<br/>from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas<br/>from PyPDF2 import PdfWriter, PdfReader<br/><br/># Create a new PDF document using reportlab<br/>c = canvas.Canvas("unsigned_document.pdf")<br/>c.drawString(100, 750, "This is a digitally unsigned document.")<br/>c.save()<br/><br/># Hypothetically instantiate PdfSignature - replace with actual implementation<br/># You may need to use another library or mix several tools, depending on requirements<br/>def sign_pdf(input_pdf_path, output_pdf_path, cert_path, cert_password):<br/>    """<br/>    Sign the PDF file using a digital certificate.<br/><br/>    :param input_pdf_path: Path to the input PDF file<br/>    :param output_pdf_path: Path to store the signed PDF<br/>    :param cert_path: Path to the digital certificate file<br/>    :param cert_password: Password for the digital certificate<br/>    """<br/>    # Read the PDF to be signed<br/>    with open(input_pdf_path, "rb") as input_pdf_file:<br/>        reader = PdfReader(input_pdf_file)<br/><br/>        # Prepare the writer<br/>        writer = PdfWriter()<br/><br/>        for page in reader.pages:<br/>            writer.add_page(page)<br/><br/>        # Normally you have to create a signature object or use a library method<br/>        # This is a pseudocode representing the signing logic<br/>        writer.add_signature(cert_path, cert_password, location="Location", reason="Reason")<br/><br/>        # Write the signed PDF<br/>        with open(output_pdf_path, "wb") as output_pdf_file:<br/>            writer.write(output_pdf_file)<br/><br/># Example usage<br/>sign_pdf("unsigned_document.pdf", "signed_document.pdf", "path/to/certificate.pem", "password")<br/>```<br/><br/>```<br/>from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas<br/>from PyPDF2 import PdfWriter, PdfReader<br/><br/># Create a new PDF document using reportlab<br/>c = canvas.Canvas("unsigned_document.pdf")<br/>c.drawString(100, 750, "This is a digitally unsigned document.")<br/>c.save()<br/><br/># Hypothetically instantiate PdfSignature - The signature is associated with the data directory CERTIFICATE\_TABLE that is not always tied to a section (it implies that the signature is not necessarily mapped in memory). In fact, the data directory entry points to a file offset, not a RVA. This signature is wrapped in a PKCS #7 container with custom object types as defined in the official documentation \[1\].<br/><br/>This signature is not new in PE files and since the beginning of LIEF, we aimed to parse it. Before the version v0.11.0, the implementation was somehow incomplete and inaccurate but since the version v0.11.0 and thanks to the sponsoring of the CERT Gouvernemental of Luxembourg, we refactored the design of the authenticode parser \[2\] and we implemented functions to verify the signature.<br/><br/>## Exploring PKCS #7 Signature¶<br/><br/>LIEF API tries to expose most of the internal components of the PKCS #7 container associated with the Authenticode. First, we can access the PE’s signature through the lief.PE.Binary.signatures attribute \[3\]:<br/><br/>import lief<br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(len(pe.signatures))<br/><br/>signature = pe.signatures[0]<br/><br/>Although we usually find only **one** signature, PE executables can embed multiple signatures thanks to the `/as` command of `signtool.exe`. This is why the signatures attribute returns an **iterator** over the signatures parsed by LIEF.<br/><br/>The signature variable is actually a lief.PE.Signature object which basically mirrors the PKCS #7 container plus some method to verify its integrity.<br/><br/>Within this object, we can access the following attributes:<br/><br/>* x509 certificates used to sign the executable: lief.PE.Signature.certificates<br/>* The ContentInfo object that contains the authentihash value: lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest<br/>* The SignerInfo structure: lief.PE.Signature.signers  <br/>Note  <br/>While the PKCS #7 standard enables multiple signers, Microsoft specifications require **one** and **only one** signer.<br/><br/>The `__str__()` functions of these objects are overloaded so that we can pretty-print the content of these objects easily:<br/><br/># Print certificates information<br/>for crt in signature.certificates:<br/>  print(crt)<br/><br/># Print the authentihash value s.r.o.<br/>  Serial Number      : 0970ef4bad5cc44a1c2bc3d96401674c<br/>  Signature Algorithm: SHA256_WITH_RSA_ENCRYPTION<br/>  Valid from         : 2020/04/02 - 00:00:00<br/>  Valid to           : OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>  Digest Algorithm    : ALGORITHMS.SHA_256<br/>  Encryption Algorithm: ALGORITHMS.RSA<br/>  Encrypted Digest    : 758db1f480eb25bada6c ...<br/>  Authenticated attributes:<br/>     Content Type OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.4 (SPC_INDIRECT_DATA_CONTENT)<br/>     MS Statement type OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.21 (INDIVIDUAL_CODE_SIGNING)<br/>     Info: http://www.avast.com<br/>     PKCS9 Message Digest: 3983816a7d1c62962540ec66fa8790fa45d1063cb23e933677de459f0b73c577<br/>  Un-authenticated attributes:<br/>     Generic Type 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1 (MS_COUNTER_SIGN)<br/><br/>## Verifying the Signature¶<br/><br/>Besides the fact that LIEF can parse PE’s authenticode signature, LIEF can also verify the integrity of the authentihash thanks to the method: lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature() which outputs lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS.OK if the signature is valid or another enum (see: lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS) when it is invalid:<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature()) # lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK<br/><br/>We can also verify a PE binary with a **detached signature** by providing a signature object to verify\_signature():<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/><br/>detached_sig = lief.PE.Signature.parse("/tmp/detached.p7b")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature(detached_sig))<br/><br/>The verification process does not rely on an external component (i.e. neither openssl nor WinTrust API) but we try to reproduce the same checks as described in the RFC(s) and the official documentation of the Authenticode \[4\].<br/><br/>These checks include:<br/><br/>1. Check the integrity of the signature (lief.PE.Signature.check()):  <br/>   1. There is ONE and only ONE SignerInfo  <br/>   2. Digest algorithms are consistent (Signature.digest\_algorithm `==` ContentInfo.digest\_algorithm `==` SignerInfo.digest\_algorithm)  <br/>   3. If the SignerInfo has authenticated attributes, check their integrity. Otherwise, check the integrity of the ContentInfo against the Signer’s certificate.  <br/>   4. If there are authenticated attributes, check that there is a lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest attribute for which the digest matches the hash of the ContentInfo  <br/>   5. If there is a counter signature in the **un-authenticated attributes**, verify its integrity and check that it wraps a valid _timestamping_.  <br/>   6. Check the expiration of the certificates according to the potential _timestamping_<br/>2. If the signature is valid, check that lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest matches the computed authentihash()<br/><br/>These checks are the default behavior of the verify\_signature(). Nevertheless, you could pass lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_CHECKS flags to customize its behavior:<br/><br/>Hash Only:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.HASH\_ONLY, it only performs step `B)` (i.e. check the authentihash values regardless of the signature integrity)<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.HASH_ONLY)<br/><br/>Lifetime Signing:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.LIFETIME\_SIGNING, timestamped signatures can expire if their certificate expired. It has the same meaning as WTD\_LIFETIME\_SIGNING\_FLAG<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/><br/>Skip Certificate Check Time:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.SKIP\_CERT\_TIME, LIEF doesn’t raise an error if the certificate(s) expired.<br/><br/># Returns lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK even though<br/># the certificates expired<br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To verify the integrity of a Signature object, you can use lief.PE.Signature.check()<br/><br/>## Certificate Chain of Trust¶<br/><br/>Last but not least, we can also verify the certificates chain thanks to:<br/><br/>1. lief.PE.x509.verify()<br/>2. lief.PE.x509.is\_trusted\_by()<br/><br/>verify() aims to verify a signed certificate from its CA. Given a CA x509 certificate, `CA.verify(signed)` verifies that the `signed` parameter has been signed by `CA`.<br/><br/>On the other hand, is\_trusted\_by() can be used to check that a given x509 certificate is verified against a **list of certificates**:<br/><br/>CA_BUNDLE = lief.PE.x509.parse("ms_bundle.pem")<br/>signer = signature.signers[0]<br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by(CA_BUNDLE))<br/><br/>cert1 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca1.crt")<br/>cert2 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca2.crt")<br/><br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by([cert1, cert2]))<br/><br/>## Limitations¶<br/><br/>Regarding the PKCS #7 structure itself, LIEF is able to parse and process most of its elements. Nevertheless, the lief.PE.SignerInfo structure can embed attributes (authenticated or not) for which the ASN.1 structure can be public or not. As of LIEF v0.11.0 we do not support yet the following OIDs:<br/><br/>\| OID                        \| Description                                                      \|<br/>\| -------------------------- \| ---------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1      \| Ms-CounterSign (undocumented, supported in LIEF 0.15.0)          \|<br/>\| 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.2.12 \| S/MIME Signing certificate (id-aa-signingCertificate)            \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.6.1      \| SPC\_COMMERCIAL\_SP\_KEY\_PURPOSE\_OBJID                         \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.28    \| szOID\_PLATFORM\_MANIFEST\_BINARY\_ID (supported in LIEF 0.15.0) \|<br/><br/>These not-supported attributes are wrapped within the lief.PE.GenericType that exposes the raw ASN.1 blob with the property raw\_content.<br/><br/>## Conclusion¶<br/><br/>Under the hood, most of the work is done by mbedtls which provides the following primitive used by LIEF:<br/><br/>* ASN.1 decoder<br/>* x509 certificate processing (parsing AND verification)<br/>* Hash algorithms<br/>* Public key algorithms<br/><br/>We can also cross-compile a small C++ snippet for iOS:<br/><br/>#include <LIEF/PE.hpp><br/><br/>int main(int argc, char** argv) \{<br/>  std::unique_ptr<LIEF::PE::Binary> pe = LIEF::PE::Parser::parse(argv[1])<br/>  if (pe->verify_signature() == LIEF::PE::Signature::VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK) \{<br/>    std::cout << "Signature ok!" << "\n";<br/>    return 0;<br/>  \}<br/>  std::cout << "Error!" << "\n";<br/>  return 1;<br/>\}<br/><br/>So that we can verify the integrity of a PE executable on an iPhone:<br/><br/>iPhone:~ root# file PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows<br/>iPhone:~ root# file ./pe_authenticode_check<br/>./pe_authenticode_check: Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, flags:<NOUNDEFS\|DYLDLINK\|TWOLEVEL\|WEAK_DEFINES\|BINDS_TO_WEAK\|PIE\|HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS><br/>iPhone:~ root# ./pe_authenticode_check PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>Signature ok!<br/>iPhone:~ root#<br/><br/>Whilst this example is quite useless, it emphasizes the purpose of this project:<br/><br/>* Provide a cross-platform and cross-format library<br/>* Expose a high-level API (Python) as well as a (more or less) low-level API (C++)<br/>* Few dependencies so that the static version of LIEF does not need external libraries \[5\].<br/><br/>$ otool -L pe_authenticode_check<br/><br/>/System/Library/Frameworks/Foundation.framework/Foundation (compatibility version 300.0.0, current version 1770.255.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 228.0.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 904.4.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1292.60.1)<br/><br/>To complete these functionalities of LIEF, you might also be interested in the following projects that deal with Authenticode:<br/><br/>\| Project          \| URL                                                                            \|<br/>\| ---------------- \| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ \|<br/>\| signify          \| <https://github.com/ralphje/signify>                                           \|<br/>\| winsign          \| <https://github.com/mozilla-releng/winsign>                                    \|<br/>\| uthenticode      \| <https://github.com/trailofbits/uthenticode>                                   \|<br/>\| AuthenticodeLint \| <https://github.com/vcsjones/AuthenticodeLint>                                 \|<br/>\| osslsigncode     \| <https://github.com/mtrojnar/osslsigncode>                                     \|<br/>\| yara-x           \| <https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x> (which has support for PE Authenticode) \|<br/><br/>Finally, you can find additional information about the Authenticode in Trail of Bits blog post \[6\]. If you are interested in Authenticode tricks used by Dropbox, you can take a look at Microsoft website \[7\] and if you are interested in understanding how the integrity of the PKCS #7 works, you can look at _Manual verify PKCS#7 signed data with OpenSSL_ \[8\]<br/><br/>References<br/><br/>\[1\]<br/><br/><http://download.microsoft.com/download/9/c/5/9c5b2167-8017-4bae-9fde-d599bac8184a/Authenticode%5FPE.docx><br/><br/>\[2\]<br/><br/>Which now exceptions-free<br/><br/>\[3\]<br/><br/>This tutorial uses the Python API but the C++ API is very similar<br/><br/>\[4\]<br/><br/>See: src/PE/signature/Signature.cpp - check() for the implementation<br/><br/>\[5\]<br/><br/>Except the C/C++ STL<br/><br/>\[6\]<br/><br/><https://blog.trailofbits.com/2020/05/27/verifying-windows-binaries-without-windows/><br/><br/>\[7\]<br/><br/><https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/ieinternals/caveats-for-authenticode-code-signing><br/><br/>\[8\]<br/><br/><http://qistoph.blogspot.com/2012/01/manual-verify-pkcs7-signed-data-with.html><br/><br/>API<br/><br/>* lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_md5<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha1<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha256<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha512<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.signatures<br/>* lief.PE.Signature<br/>* lief.PE.x509<br/>* lief.PE.ContentInfo<br/>* lief.PE.SignerInfo<br/>* lief.PE.Attribute<br/>* lief.PE.ContentType<br/>* lief.PE.GenericType<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcNestedSignature<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcStatementType<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9AtSequenceNumber<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9CounterSignature<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9SigningTime<br/>* lief.PE.SpcSpOpusInfo<br/><br/> On this page: IntroductionExploring PKCS #7 SignatureVerifying the SignatureCertificate Chain of TrustLimitationsConclusion |

The signature is associated with the data directory CERTIFICATE\_TABLEthat is not always tied to a section (it implies that the signature is not necessarily mapped in memory). In fact, the data directory entry points to a file offset, not a RVA. This signature is wrapped in a PKCS #7 container with custom object types as defined in the official documentation \[1\].<br/><br/>This signature is not new in PE files and since the beginning of LIEF, we aimed to parse it. Before the version v0.11.0, the implementation was somehow incomplete and inaccurate but since the version v0.11.0 and thanks to the sponsoring of the CERT Gouvernemental of Luxembourg, we refactored the design of the authenticode parser \[2\] and we implemented functions to verify the signature.<br/><br/>## Exploring PKCS #7 Signature¶<br/><br/>LIEF API tries to expose most of the internal components of the PKCS #7 container associated with the Authenticode. First, we can access the PE’s signature through the lief.PE.Binary.signatures attribute\[3\]:<br/><br/>import lief<br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(len(pe.signatures))<br/><br/>signature = pe.signatures[0]<br/><br/>Although we usually find only **one** signature, PE executables can embed multiple signatures thanks to the `/as` command of `signtool.exe`. This is why the signatures attribute returns an**iterator** over the signatures parsed by LIEF.<br/><br/>The signature variable is actually a lief.PE.Signature object which basically mirrors the PKCS #7 container plus some method to verify its integrity.<br/><br/>Within this object, we can access the following attributes:<br/><br/>* x509 certificates used to sign the executable: lief.PE.Signature.certificates<br/>* The ContentInfo object that contains the authentihash value: lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest<br/>* The SignerInfo structure: lief.PE.Signature.signers  <br/>Note  <br/>While the PKCS #7 standard enables multiple signers, Microsoft specifications require **one** and **only one**signer.<br/><br/>The `__str__()` functions of these objects are overloaded so that we can pretty-print the content of these objects easily:<br/><br/># Print certificates information<br/>for crt in signature.certificates:<br/>  print(crt)<br/><br/># Print the authentihash value embedded in the signature<br/>print(signature.content_info.digest.hex())<br/><br/># Print signer information<br/>print(signature.signers[0])<br/><br/>cert. version     : 3<br/>serial number     : 04:09:18:1B:5F:D5:BB:66:75:53:43:B5:6F:95:50:08<br/>issuer name       : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert Assured ID Root CA<br/>subject name      : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>issued  on        : 2013-10-22 12:00:00<br/>expires on        : 2028-10-22 12:00:00<br/>signed using      : RSA with SHA-256<br/>RSA key size      : 2048 bits<br/>basic constraints : CA=true, max_pathlen=0<br/>key usage         : Digital Signature, Key Cert Sign, CRL Sign<br/>ext key usage     : Code Signing<br/><br/>cert. version     : 3<br/>serial number     : 09:70:EF:4B:AD:5C:C4:4A:1C:2B:C3:D9:64:01:67:4C<br/>issuer name       : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>subject name      : C=CZ, L=Praha, O=Avast Software s.r.o., OU=RE stapler cistodc, CN=Avast Software s.r.o.<br/>issued  on        : 2020-04-02 00:00:00<br/>expires on        : 2023-03-09 12:00:00<br/>signed using      : RSA with SHA-256<br/>RSA key size      : 2048 bits<br/>basic constraints : CA=false<br/>key usage         : Digital Signature<br/>ext key usage     : Code Signing<br/><br/>a738da4446a4e78ab647db7e53427eb07961c994317f4c59d7edbea5cc786d80<br/>SHA_256/RSA - C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA - 4 auth attr - 1 unauth attr<br/><br/>Regarding the PE files, the authentihash is computed through the function lief.PE.Binary.authentihash()which takes a lief.PE.ALGORITHMS enum as parameter to define which hash algorithm must be used to compute the digest.<br/><br/>For instance, to compute the SHA-256 value of the authenticode, we just have to pass lief.PE.ALGORITHMS.SHA\_256:<br/><br/>print(pe.authentihash(lief.PE.ALGORITHMS.SHA_256).hex())<br/><br/>a738da4446a4e78ab647db7e53427eb07961c994317f4c59d7edbea5cc786d80<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To compare the lief.PE.Binary.authentihash() value with the signed one (i.e. lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest) we must use the same hash algorithm as defined by lief.PE.Signature.digest\_algorithm<br/><br/>We also expose shortcut attributes in the Python API to compute the authentihash values for:<br/><br/>\| Hash Algorithm \| Binary’s Attribute                                                                                                          \|<br/>\| -------------- \| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| MD5            \| [authentihash\_md5](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fmd5 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_md5")          \|<br/>\| SHA1           \| [authentihash\_sha1](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha1 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha1")       \|<br/>\| SHA-256        \| [authentihash\_sha256](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha256 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha256") \|<br/>\| SHA-512        \| [authentihash\_sha512](../formats/pe/python.html#lief.PE.Binary.authentihash%5Fsha512 "lief.PE.Binary.authentihash_sha512") \|<br/><br/>LIEF also exposes the original raw signature blob through the property lief.PE.Signature.raw\_der which enables to export the signature:<br/><br/>from pathlib import Path<br/><br/>Path("/tmp/extracted.p7b").write_bytes(signature.raw_der)<br/><br/>Then, we can use `openssl` to process its content:<br/><br/>$ openssl pkcs7 -inform der -print -in /tmp/extracted.p7b -noout -text<br/>...<br/>     sig_alg:<br/>       algorithm: sha256WithRSAEncryption located in the examples/ directory can also be used to inspect the signature:<br/><br/>$ python authenticode_reader.py --all avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe<br/><br/>Signature version : 1<br/>Digest Algorithm  : ALGORITHMS.SHA_256<br/>Content Info:<br/>  Content Type    : 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.4 (SPC_INDIRECT_DATA_CONTENT)<br/>  Digest Algorithm: ALGORITHMS.SHA_256<br/>  Digest          : a738da4446a4e78ab647db7e53427eb07961c994317f4c59d7edbea5cc786d80<br/>Certificates<br/>  Version            : 3<br/>  Issuer             : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert Assured ID Root CA<br/>  Subject            : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>  Serial Number      : 0409181b5fd5bb66755343b56f955008<br/>  Signature Algorithm: SHA256_WITH_RSA_ENCRYPTION<br/>  Valid from         : 2013/10/22 - 12:00:00<br/>  Valid to           : 2028/10/22 - 12:00:00<br/>  Key usage          : CRL_SIGN - KEY_CERT_SIGN - DIGITAL_SIGNATURE<br/>  Ext key usage      : CODE_SIGNING<br/>  RSA key size       : 2048<br/>  ===========================================<br/>  Version            : 3<br/>  Issuer             : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>  Subject            : C=CZ, L=Praha, O=Avast Software s.r.o., OU=RE stapler cistodc, CN=Avast Software s.r.o.<br/>  Serial Number      : 0970ef4bad5cc44a1c2bc3d96401674c<br/>  Signature Algorithm: SHA256_WITH_RSA_ENCRYPTION<br/>  Valid from         : 2020/04/02 - 00:00:00<br/>  Valid to           : 2023/03/09 - 12:00:00<br/>  Key usage          : DIGITAL_SIGNATURE<br/>  Ext key usage      : CODE_SIGNING<br/>  RSA key size       : 2048<br/>  ===========================================<br/>Signer(s)<br/>  Version             : 1<br/>  Serial Number       : 0970ef4bad5cc44a1c2bc3d96401674c<br/>  Issuer              : C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert SHA2 Assured ID Code Signing CA<br/>  Digest Algorithm    : ALGORITHMS.SHA_256<br/>  Encryption Algorithm: ALGORITHMS.RSA<br/>  Encrypted Digest    : 758db1f480eb25bada6c ...<br/>  Authenticated attributes:<br/>     Content Type OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.4 (SPC_INDIRECT_DATA_CONTENT)<br/>     MS Statement type OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.21 (INDIVIDUAL_CODE_SIGNING)<br/>     Info: http://www.avast.com<br/>     PKCS9 Message Digest: 3983816a7d1c62962540ec66fa8790fa45d1063cb23e933677de459f0b73c577<br/>  Un-authenticated attributes:<br/>     Generic Type 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1 (MS_COUNTER_SIGN)<br/><br/>## Verifying the Signature¶<br/><br/>Besides the fact that LIEF can parse PE’s authenticode signature, LIEF can also verify the integrity of the authentihash thanks to the method: lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature() which outputs lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS.OKif the signature is valid or another enum (see: lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_FLAGS) when it is invalid:<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature()) # lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK<br/><br/>We can also verify a PE binary with a **detached signature** by providing a signatureobject to verify\_signature():<br/><br/>pe = lief.parse("avast_free_antivirus_setup_online.exe")<br/><br/>detached_sig = lief.PE.Signature.parse("/tmp/detached.p7b")<br/>print(pe.verify_signature(detached_sig))<br/><br/>The verification process does not rely on an external component (i.e. neither openssl nor WinTrust API) but we try to reproduce the same checks as described in the RFC(s) and the official documentation of the Authenticode\[4\].<br/><br/>These checks include:<br/><br/>1. Check the integrity of the signature (lief.PE.Signature.check()):  <br/>   1. There is ONE and only ONE SignerInfo  <br/>   2. Digest algorithms are consistent (Signature.digest\_algorithm `==` ContentInfo.digest\_algorithm `==` SignerInfo.digest\_algorithm)  <br/>   3. If the SignerInfo has authenticated attributes, check their integrity. Otherwise, check the integrity of the ContentInfo against the Signer’s certificate.  <br/>   4. If there are authenticated attributes, check that there is alief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest attribute for which the digestmatches the hash of the ContentInfo  <br/>   5. If there is a counter signature in the **un-authenticated attributes**, verify its integrity and check that it wraps a valid _timestamping_.  <br/>   6. Check the expiration of the certificates according to the potential _timestamping_<br/>2. If the signature is valid, check that lief.PE.ContentInfo.digest matches the computedauthentihash()<br/><br/>These checks are the default behavior of the verify\_signature(). Nevertheless, you could pass lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION\_CHECKS flags to customize its behavior:<br/><br/>Hash Only:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.HASH\_ONLY, it only performs step `B)` (i.e. check the authentihash values regardless of the signature integrity)<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.HASH_ONLY)<br/><br/>Lifetime Signing:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.LIFETIME\_SIGNING, timestamped signatures can expire if their certificate expired. It has the same meaning as WTD\_LIFETIME\_SIGNING\_FLAG<br/><br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.LIFETIME_SIGNING)<br/><br/>Skip Certificate Check Time:<br/><br/>By using VERIFICATION\_CHECKS.SKIP\_CERT\_TIME, LIEF doesn’t raise an error if the certificate(s) expired.<br/><br/># Returns lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK even though<br/># the certificates expired<br/>pe.verify_signature(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/>signature.check(lief.PE.Signature.VERIFICATION_CHECKS.SKIP_CERT_TIME)<br/><br/>Note<br/><br/>To verify the integrity of a Signature object, you can uselief.PE.Signature.check()<br/><br/>## Certificate Chain of Trust¶<br/><br/>Last but not least, we can also verify the certificates chain thanks to:<br/><br/>1. lief.PE.x509.verify()<br/>2. lief.PE.x509.is\_trusted\_by()<br/><br/>verify() aims to verify a signed certificate from its CA. Given a CA x509certificate, `CA.verify(signed)` verifies that the `signed` parameter has been signed by `CA`.<br/><br/>On the other hand, is\_trusted\_by() can be used to check that a given x509certificate is verified against a **list of certificates**:<br/><br/>CA_BUNDLE = lief.PE.x509.parse("ms_bundle.pem")<br/>signer = signature.signers[0]<br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by(CA_BUNDLE))<br/><br/>cert1 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca1.crt")<br/>cert2 = lief.PE.x509.parse("ca2.crt")<br/><br/>print(signer.cert.is_trusted_by([cert1, cert2]))<br/><br/>## Limitations¶<br/><br/>Regarding the PKCS #7 structure itself, LIEF is able to parse and process most of its elements. Nevertheless, the lief.PE.SignerInfo structure can embed attributes (authenticated or not) for which the ASN.1 structure can be public or not. As of LIEF v0.11.0 we do not support yet the following OIDs:<br/><br/>\| OID                        \| Description                                                      \|<br/>\| -------------------------- \| ---------------------------------------------------------------- \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1      \| Ms-CounterSign (undocumented, supported in LIEF 0.15.0)          \|<br/>\| 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.2.12 \| S/MIME Signing certificate (id-aa-signingCertificate)            \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.6.1      \| SPC\_COMMERCIAL\_SP\_KEY\_PURPOSE\_OBJID                         \|<br/>\| 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.28    \| szOID\_PLATFORM\_MANIFEST\_BINARY\_ID (supported in LIEF 0.15.0) \|<br/><br/>These not-supported attributes are wrapped within the lief.PE.GenericType that exposes the raw ASN.1 blob with the property raw\_content.<br/><br/>## Conclusion¶<br/><br/>Under the hood, most of the work is done by mbedtls which provides the following primitive used by LIEF:<br/><br/>* ASN.1 decoder<br/>* x509 certificate processing (parsing AND verification)<br/>* Hash algorithms<br/>* Public key algorithms<br/><br/>We can also cross-compile a small C++ snippet for iOS:<br/><br/>#include <LIEF/PE.hpp><br/><br/>int main(int argc, char** argv) \{<br/>  std::unique_ptr<LIEF::PE::Binary> pe = LIEF::PE::Parser::parse(argv[1])<br/>  if (pe->verify_signature() == LIEF::PE::Signature::VERIFICATION_FLAGS.OK) \{<br/>    std::cout << "Signature ok!" << "\n";<br/>    return 0;<br/>  \}<br/>  std::cout << "Error!" << "\n";<br/>  return 1;<br/>\}<br/><br/>So that we can verify the integrity of a PE executable on an iPhone:<br/><br/>iPhone:~ root# file PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows<br/>iPhone:~ root# file ./pe_authenticode_check<br/>./pe_authenticode_check: Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, flags:<NOUNDEFS\|DYLDLINK\|TWOLEVEL\|WEAK_DEFINES\|BINDS_TO_WEAK\|PIE\|HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS><br/>iPhone:~ root# ./pe_authenticode_check PE32_x86-64_binary_avast-free-antivirus-setup-online.exe<br/>Signature ok!<br/>iPhone:~ root#<br/><br/>Whilst this example is quite useless, it emphasizes the purpose of this project:<br/><br/>* Provide a cross-platform and cross-format library<br/>* Expose a high-level API (Python) as well as a (more or less) low-level API (C++)<br/>* Few dependencies so that the static version of LIEF does not need external libraries \[5\].<br/><br/>$ otool -L pe_authenticode_check<br/><br/>/System/Library/Frameworks/Foundation.framework/Foundation (compatibility version 300.0.0, current version 1770.255.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 228.0.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 904.4.0)<br/>/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1292.60.1)<br/><br/>To complete these functionalities of LIEF, you might also be interested in the following projects that deal with Authenticode:<br/><br/>\| Project          \| URL                                                                            \|<br/>\| ---------------- \| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ \|<br/>\| signify          \| <https://github.com/ralphje/signify>                                           \|<br/>\| winsign          \| <https://github.com/mozilla-releng/winsign>                                    \|<br/>\| uthenticode      \| <https://github.com/trailofbits/uthenticode>                                   \|<br/>\| AuthenticodeLint \| <https://github.com/vcsjones/AuthenticodeLint>                                 \|<br/>\| osslsigncode     \| <https://github.com/mtrojnar/osslsigncode>                                     \|<br/>\| yara-x           \| <https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x> (which has support for PE Authenticode) \|<br/><br/>Finally, you can find additional information about the Authenticode in Trail of Bits blog post \[6\]. If you are interested in Authenticode tricks used by Dropbox, you can take a look at Microsoft website \[7\] and if you are interested in understanding how the integrity of the PKCS #7 works, you can look at _Manual verify PKCS#7 signed data with OpenSSL_ \[8\]<br/><br/>References<br/><br/>\[1\] <br/><br/><http://download.microsoft.com/download/9/c/5/9c5b2167-8017-4bae-9fde-d599bac8184a/Authenticode%5FPE.docx><br/><br/>\[2\] <br/><br/>Which now exceptions-free<br/><br/>\[3\] <br/><br/>This tutorial uses the Python API but the C++ API is very similar<br/><br/>\[4\] <br/><br/>See: src/PE/signature/Signature.cpp - check() for the implementation<br/><br/>\[5\] <br/><br/>Except the C/C++ STL<br/><br/>\[6\] <br/><br/><https://blog.trailofbits.com/2020/05/27/verifying-windows-binaries-without-windows/><br/><br/>\[7\] <br/><br/><https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/ieinternals/caveats-for-authenticode-code-signing><br/><br/>\[8\] <br/><br/><http://qistoph.blogspot.com/2012/01/manual-verify-pkcs7-signed-data-with.html><br/><br/>API<br/><br/>* lief.PE.Binary.verify\_signature()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash()<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_md5<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha1<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha256<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.authentihash\_sha512<br/>* lief.PE.Binary.signatures<br/>* lief.PE.Signature<br/>* lief.PE.x509<br/>* lief.PE.ContentInfo<br/>* lief.PE.SignerInfo<br/>* lief.PE.Attribute<br/>* lief.PE.ContentType<br/>* lief.PE.GenericType<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcNestedSignature<br/>* lief.PE.MsSpcStatementType<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9AtSequenceNumber<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9CounterSignature<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9MessageDigest<br/>* lief.PE.PKCS9SigningTime<br/>* lief.PE.SpcSpOpusInfo<br/><br/> On this page: Introduction Exploring PKCS #7 Signature Verifying the Signature Certificate Chain of Trust Limitations Conclusion |
